title: What goes in, what comes back
caption: A function is a deal about two things: what it is handed, and what it hands back. Printing is not handing back — it puts the number where only a person can see it, and the caller gets None. Defaults are settled once, when the def line runs, which is why a list left as a default is shared by every call that omits it.

cells.label: argument
cells.note: a name for what the caller handed over. Exists only during the call

cells.label: return
cells.note: hands a value back. trays_needed(310) is 26, and 26 can be added to something

cells.label: print
cells.note: shows it and hands back None. None + None is a TypeError

cells.label: default
cells.note: used when the caller says nothing. Worked out once, at def — so never a list
